name: music.render
title: Music render (Strudel)
summary: Render a Strudel song to audio with the Mucavex engine: seeded deterministic noise, named section markers and the song's form, optional stems of named parts, a tempo override and an analysis report.
description: Evaluates Strudel live-coding JavaScript with the same semantics as the strudel.cc REPL and renders it offline to WAV/MP3/FLAC/OGG/Opus/M4A. Named markers (lines like `let DROP = 34;`) let a build move song sections without regenerating the code, and `markers_found` reports the song's form: every numeric marker with the time it lands at (markers count cycles from 0, so at_s = value / cps). `stems` renders named parts (`drums: s("bd*4")`, or `$:` lines by order) to separate files in the same job: each stem is the song again with every other part muted, so a stem costs a render of its own (`stems_only` skips the full mix). Strudel noise is seeded, so identical input gives byte-identical audio. `max_polyphony` must stay high: the engine's old default of 128 steals voices and fades sample voices in long renders. The tool renders; it applies no loudness normalisation, ducking or limiting of its own (`peak_db` is the only gain it will add, and only when asked). It always measures the render's sample peak, warns when an over-hot render would be clamped by the chosen format, and never clips silently. It also measures how loud each part of the render is: `levels` has the RMS level of every cycle of the song and each entry of `markers_found` the level of its section, because a render can succeed with every marker in place and still be a few bars of music and then one stuck tone. When most cycles sit at one level a warning says so; it is a hint to check the render, never an error (a drone or an unchanging loop gets it too).

code.description: Strudel source as a string. Exactly one of `code` and `file` is required.

file.description: A workspace `.strudel` or `.js` file holding the song: a workspace path, job:<id>/<output> or pin:<name>. Exactly one of `code` and `file` is required.

markers.description: Rewrite named marker lines (`let NAME = value;`) before rendering, e.g. {"DROP": 30}. An unknown name is an invalid-input error that lists the markers found in the song.

seconds.description: Render this many seconds. Wins over `cycles`. Omit both for the engine default of 4 cycles.

cycles.description: Render this many Strudel cycles. Omit both `cycles` and `seconds` for the engine default of 4.

cps.description: Cycles per second. Wins over `bpm`. Omit both to let the song's setcps/setcpm decide.

bpm.description: Beats per minute; converted with cps = bpm / 60 / beats_per_cycle. Omit (with `cps`) to let the song decide.

beats_per_cycle.description: Beats in one cycle, used only when `bpm` is given. 4 means one cycle is a 4/4 bar.

tail_s.description: Extra seconds after the last cycle so reverb and release tails are not cut off.

format.description: Output container/codec. wav is 16-bit PCM, wav32 is 32-bit float (the only format that keeps overs above 0 dBFS); flac/ogg/opus/m4a need ffmpeg. Every other format clamps past ±1.0, which distorts an over-hot render.

bitrate_k.description: Bitrate in kbps for lossy formats (mp3, opus, m4a). Omit for the encoder default.

peak_db.description: Scale the whole render by one gain so its sample peak lands exactly at this dBFS (for example -1), applied before encoding so nothing clips. Omit to leave the render untouched. `gain_db_applied` reports the gain used. A silent render is not scaled (it gets a warning instead). With `stems`, every stem gets the same gain as the mix, so the stems keep their balance.

max_polyphony.description: Maximum simultaneous voices. Keep this high: Strudel's default of 128 steals voices, which fades earlier sample voices in long renders. Raise it further for very dense songs.

seed.description: Seed for the Math.random replacement Strudel noise uses. The same seed gives byte-identical audio; change it for a different noise take.

analyze.description: Also measure the render (peak/RMS/crest/clipping/warnings) and write analysis.json.

offline.description: Only load samples from the sample cache, never the network. A missing sample then fails the render instead of downloading it.

name.description: Output file name for the rendered audio. Default music.<ext>. The extension always follows format (a given .wav/.mp3/... is replaced), e.g. name "score" with format mp3 writes score.mp3.

items.description: A part of the song: a label as written (`drums` for `drums: s("bd*4")` or `.p('drums')`; every statement with that label), or `$1`, `$2`, ... for the anonymous `$:` parts, counted in song order (a muted `_$:` line counts too).

additionalProperties.description: The parts this stem keeps audible.

stems.description: Also render named parts of the song to separate files, e.g. {"drums": ["kick", "hats"], "bass": ["bass"], "lead": ["$1"]}. After the full mix, the song is rendered once more per stem with every part outside the stem muted (the Strudel `_` mute), written to stems/<stem name>.<ext> (and the muted song to stems/<stem name>.strudel) with the same format, length, tail, seed and sample rate. Each stem is a full render, so stems multiply the render time. Unlabelled statements are not parts (Strudel does not play them once a song has labelled parts). An unknown or muted part is invalid-input that lists the parts found in the song. Omit for no stems.

stems_only.description: With `stems`, skip the full mix: only the stems are rendered (no music.<ext>, no analysis.json, `analysis` and `peak_db` are null). Saves one render. Cannot be combined with `peak_db`, which scales by the full mix's peak. Omit (or false) to render the full mix too.

seconds.description: Rendered duration in seconds, including the tail.

events.description: Number of note/trigger events rendered in the full mix (with stems_only: summed over the stem renders).

render_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds spent rendering the audio, the full mix and every stem together.

markers_found.description: The song's form: every marker line in the rendered code (after `markers` rewrites) whose value is a number, or arithmetic over numbers and earlier markers (`let OUTRO = DROP + 8;`), in file order. Lines holding anything else (functions, patterns, strings) are not listed.

value.description: The marker's value in cycles, or its text when it uses a name that is not a marker (then at_s and bar are absent).

expression.description: The text the value was computed from, when it is not a plain number (e.g. "DROP + 8").

at_s.description: Seconds from the start of the render where the marker lands: value / cps. Markers count Strudel cycles from 0 (the convention in the music guide).

bar.description: The same value read as a bar counted from 0, assuming one cycle is one bar (what beats_per_cycle means): bar 6 is the 7th bar.

rms_db.description: RMS level in dBFS of the written full mix (mono sum, after any `peak_db` scaling) from this marker to the next marker in time, or to the end of the song (the tail is left out); null when that stretch is digital silence. Every numeric marker line counts as a next marker, also one that is not a section. Absent when there is nothing to measure: the marker lands outside the song (before 0, or at or after its end), its value is not a number, or stems_only skipped the full mix.

levels.description: How loud each cycle of the song is in the written full mix, in order from cycle 0; the tail (`tail_s`) is left out. One row per cycle for songs of up to 256 cycles; a longer song gets rows of N whole cycles each, with the smallest N that keeps the array at 256 rows or fewer (consecutive `cycle` values then step by N). A song that ends inside a cycle has a shorter last row. Null when stems_only skipped the full mix. Read it after every render, also a re-render: a part that drops out, or a stuck note, shows here and nowhere else in the result.

cycle.description: The cycle the row starts at, counted from 0 like the markers (with one cycle per bar, cycle 6 is the 7th bar).

at_s.description: Seconds from the start of the render where the row starts: cycle / cps.

to_s.description: Seconds where the row ends: the start of the next row, or the end of the song for the last one.

rms_db.description: RMS level in dBFS of the mono sum of the file as written (after any `peak_db` scaling, and clamped at full scale when the format clamps an over-hot render), over the whole row; null for digital silence.

stems.description: One entry per requested stem, in request order. Present only when `stems` was given.

file.description: Output path of the stem audio, e.g. stems/drums.wav (job:<id>/stems/drums.wav).

parts.description: The part selectors this stem kept audible, as requested.

lines.description: 1-based lines of the statements the stem kept audible, to check that $N is the part you meant.

peak_db.description: Sample peak of the written stem in dBFS (after the mix's peak_db gain, if any), or null when the stem is silent.

render_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds spent rendering this stem.

markers_applied.description: Markers that were rewritten, in request order.

value.description: Value written into the marker line.

peak_db.description: Sample peak of the written render in dBFS (after any `peak_db` scaling), or null when the render is silent or stems_only skipped the full mix.

gain_db_applied.description: Gain in dB applied to reach `peak_db` (to the mix and every stem), or null when no scaling was requested (or the render is silent).

analysis.description: Analysis of the full mix, or null when analyze is false or stems_only skipped the mix.

peakDb.description: Absolute sample peak in dBFS (-Infinity serialises as null by JSON).

clippedSamples.description: Samples at or above full scale.

warnings.description: Human-readable warnings: events the engine could not play (unknown sound names, failed sample loads), a sample file that had to be decoded through ffmpeg, a render that peaks above 0 dBFS in a format that clamps, a silent render asked to reach `peak_db`, and a flat render: when `levels` has at least 8 rows and at least three quarters of all rows are audible (-50 dBFS or louder) and within 1 dB of each other, the warning gives the count and the level, because that is what a stuck note looks like (a drone or an unchanging loop reads the same; silent rows count against the share and have the analysis warnings of their own). A stem's own warnings start with `stem "<name>": `, and a song that solos parts (labels starting with S) is named, because Strudel then leaves the other parts out. Empty when nothing went wrong.

examples.title: Two cycles of a sawtooth triad, offline
A lead and a bass as two stems, and the bar where the bass enters (synths only, offline)

input.code:
let BASS = 1; // the bass enters at cycle 1
lead: note("c4 e4 g4 e4").s("square").lpf(1200).gain(0.25)
bass: note("c2*2").s("sawtooth").lpf(300).mask(cat(...Array(BASS).fill(0), 1))
